questions.question: A test calls `await page.screenshot({ path: 'home.png' })` and the page's layout is badly broken. What happens?
options: The test fails with a pixel difference
The test passes, because `page.screenshot()` only saves an image
Playwright retries until the layout is fixed
The test fails because no baseline exists
questions.explanation: `page.screenshot()` makes no comparison. Use `await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot()` to fail on visual changes.

questions.question: You run a new `toHaveScreenshot('home.png')` assertion for the first time. What happens?
options: The test passes and no file is written
The test is skipped until you pass `--update-snapshots`
Playwright writes the baseline and fails the test
Playwright downloads a baseline from the last CI run
questions.explanation: With no baseline to compare, Playwright writes the capture and fails on purpose so you review the image before committing it.

questions.question: What does `threshold: 0.2` control in `toHaveScreenshot()`?
options: Up to 20% of the image's pixels may differ
How different one pixel's perceived color must be before it counts as changed
The test may take 20% longer than the timeout
Each color channel may change by exactly 20%
questions.explanation: `threshold` is a per-pixel perceived color difference. `maxDiffPixels` and `maxDiffPixelRatio` limit how many changed pixels are allowed.

questions.question: A screenshot test passes on your Mac, but CI on Ubuntu reports that its baseline is missing or different. What is the best fix?
options: Set `maxDiffPixelRatio: 1` for every assertion
Delete the platform from the file name and share the Mac image
Create the baselines in the same environment that CI uses
Run the test with `--ignore-snapshots` in CI
questions.explanation: Fonts and rendering differ between systems. Generating baselines in the CI job or matching Docker image keeps comparisons meaningful.

questions.question: A dashboard shows a live timestamp that you can control from the test. What is the best way to keep the screenshot stable?
options: Freeze the time with `page.clock.setFixedTime()`
Add a long `waitForTimeout()` before the screenshot
Raise `maxDiffPixels` until the test passes
Set `animations: 'allow'`
questions.explanation: Freezing the input keeps the timestamp in the image and still tests how it renders. Mask it only when you can't control it.
